title: TailLoR: Protecting Principal Components in Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
abstract: Parameter-efficient finetuning methods based on spectral decomposition have enabled progress in Continual Learning. In this paper we introduce TailLoR, which utilizes the singular bases U and V of the pre-trained weights as a fixed reference frame to learn a low-rank update applied to the singular value matrix. A soft spectral penalty discourages updates aligned with dominant singular directions, reducing interference while routing fine-grained adaptation into the highly flexible, long-tail spectral coordinates.

significance.justification: The paper introduces TailLoR which refines parameter-efficient finetuning for continual learning by protecting principal components while enabling adaptation in less dominant directions, offering measurable gains for builders implementing continual learning systems.

novelty.justification: TailLoR presents a substantial new variation by utilizing singular bases as a fixed reference frame and applying a soft spectral penalty to route adaptation into long-tail spectral coordinates, distinct from prior spectral decomposition approaches.

reproducibility.justification: The method is described clearly enough to reimplement with spectral decomposition and soft penalty techniques, but no mention of code, weights, or datasets being publicly available.

clarity.justification: The abstract is well-written and clearly explains the core contribution of using singular bases as a reference frame with spectral penalty for continual learning adaptation.

topical_fit.justification: Directly in the LLM and applied-AI sweet spot as it addresses parameter-efficient finetuning methods for continual learning, a core concern for builders working with LLMs.
